result.title: LaWanle: Why Can't Leading Driving Models Make a Simple Turn?
result.summary: We were surprised to find that leading end-to-end driving models across major paradigms, despite scoring close to human drivers on NAVSIM, cannot reliably make a simple 90-degree turn in photorealistic closed-loop simulators. To investigate why, we build LaWanle, a benchmark of turns drawn from three such simulators. Driving each turn from several starts, we find that the same model passes it from one start and fails it from another, and that the two drives look alike until they enter the junction. Rotating the car by a few degrees at the junction entry can fail a turn it otherwise passes. Conversely, a slight heading correction to the plans can rescue about half of the failed turns we tested. Such errors arise when a model drives by itself, so we post-train an open-source lane-keeping model with closed-loop DAgger on its lateral path. Training 5% of its parameters is enough to raise its turn pass rate from 19% to 76%. The gain transfers to the two other benchmarks, where the policy also scores among the leading models. Further fine-tuning on recovery data repairs the deviations it is trained on but, against a control trained equally long, improves turns on none of the three benchmarks, and every variant stays far below a human driver.

AI.brief_summary: 论文构建了来自三个真实感闭环模拟器的 90 度转弯基准，发现 NAVSIM 上接近人类水平的端到端驾驶模型在同一转弯的不同起点上成败不一，入口处几度朝向偏差即可致其失败；随后用闭环 DAgger 对开源车道保持模型的横向路径做后训练，仅训练 5% 参数即把通过率从 19% 提升到 76%。
AI.relevance_reason: 「入口微小朝向扰动即致失败」与「恢复数据微调相对等时长对照无改善」这两点，可能为 LVR 中几何与任务必要细节是否保留在内部状态、以及轨迹级监督能否纠错状态提供可核查的评测线索，但领域距离较远，需较多核查。
